extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, STIC staff, and other USPTO personnel involved in prior-art searching and classification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO patent examiners on obtaining and using foreign patent and non‑patent literature, translation services, STIC collections and services, and classification resources/tools to perform complete and accurate prior‑art searches and classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required bibliographic data for design records (INID codes 72–88)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify applicant(s) (72), creator(s) if known (73), owner(s) name(s) and address(es) (73/74), representative(s) (74), new owner(s) in case of change (78), and data related to international deposits and conventions (80). Designated State(s)/States concerned fields (81,82,84) and owner information (86–88) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration occurred on or before the date the industrial design was made available to the public, indicating the owner(s) meets the minimum data requirement; otherwise indicate the applicant(s). Data for INID codes (81)–(88) should use two-letter WIPO ST.3 country codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for obtaining foreign patent copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may obtain copies of foreign patents and published specifications from STIC, Technology Center, or automated search tools (EAST, WEST, FPAS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STIC can retrieve copies from its collection or from the originating patent office; unprinted documents should include reported grant and public-availability dates. Examiners may order copies from their TC or STIC, or make copies themselves. Current documents accessible via USPTO automated systems; older documents available on microfilm or print in STIC Main Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical placement and selection of foreign family members in search files
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to October 1, 1995, only a single patent family member was placed in examiner search files; non-English documents were accompanied, when possible, by English abstracts; for countries that printed specifications twice, generally only the first printing was placed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be aware of historical file completeness and consider equivalents or later family members when relevant; STIC staff check for equivalents before processing translation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation request and usage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may consult Translations Branch translators for oral assistance and may request written translations of pertinent portions or full translations of foreign documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged to use oral assistance and language reference resources early in examination; written translations can be requested at any point but Translations Branch will check for existing equivalents/translations first. Since Jan 1, 2004 written translations are delivered by e-mail only; submit only copies of foreign documents for translation and retain originals. Translation requests may be submitted electronically, by phone, or fax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for equivalents and prior translations before requesting new translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations Branch staff check for family-equivalent documents or previously made translations prior to processing a new translation request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should search for preferred‑language equivalents and previously translated versions; Translations Branch maintains a database of over 30,000 translations indexed by country/patent or language/author/title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and citation of non‑patent literature (NPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: All printed publications may be used as references; citation date is the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STIC maintains Electronic Information Centers; see MPEP § 2128–2128.02 for citation format and MPEP § 707.05(e) for how to cite such publications. Use the publication date as the date to be cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and purpose of STIC collections
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC maintains comprehensive collections of foreign patents, technical literature, reference works, periodicals, and specialized collections (e.g., Biotechnology/Chemical and Law Library) to assist examiners in determining anticipation and obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections are primarily English-language purchases, with electronic access emphasized. Reference materials do not circulate; locations and holdings are recorded in the STIC Online Catalog. Examiners may request items to be located in Technology Centers when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition and purchase requests for STIC materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may request purchases of books, periodicals, and database subscriptions for STIC and Technology Center collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests are accepted anytime; purchases depend on demonstrated need and funding availability. STIC solicits suggestions from the Examining Corps for additional acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and organization of periodicals and indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 17,000 periodical titles (print and electronic) are available; foreign official journals and indexes are shelved under country names and much index info is available on FPAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current print issues are shelved alphabetically; bound periodicals are interfiled with books; microfilm and CD-ROM holdings are stored in cabinets. Some foreign journals include abstracts of patent disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Patent Services offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign Patent and Scientific Literature Branch provides patent family searches, preferred-language equivalents, determination of priority and publication dates, inventor-name or abstract-number searches, patent family/bibliographic searches, and foreign classification information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff also train examiners in using FPAS and assist in locating foreign patent collections and indexes. Members of the public can order copies of foreign patent documents from this branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online database searching and STIC search services
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC provides online searching via vendor databases (e.g., DIALOG, STN, Questel‑Orbit) and offers search-request services; completed searches typically delivered in two working days or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may request computer searches electronically or on paper. Examiners can conduct vendor database searches independently after SPE approval and training; STIC provides training and individual assistance, especially for chemical-structure and DNA-sequence searches. Sequence searches for nucleic/amino acids are performed via an in‑house system by the Biotechnology/Chemical Information Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlibrary loan policy
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC will borrow materials not available in-house for official business purposes via interlibrary loan requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests submitted to the STIC facility in the examiner's TC or via electronic form; local metropolitan requests handled by Reference Delivery Branch; remote requests routed electronically through networks/vendors. Law books cannot be borrowed by STIC for use in law courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site photocopying of STIC materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Photocopy machines in STIC are available for examiner use to copy STIC materials that do not circulate or materials examiners choose not to check out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use machines for noncirculating reference items or convenience copying; observe any STIC policies on handling and returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for obtaining publication dates of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to determine earliest publication or first distribution dates should be made to STIC in the examiner's Technology Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For U.S. publications, STIC staff can obtain the day and month claimed by the copyright owner; similar information for foreign publications can be obtained through correspondence but may take longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and citation of Alien Property Custodian (A.P.C.) publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A.P.C. published applications (vested during WWII and published even though not granted) should be designated as A.P.C. published applications, not patents, and are usable as printed publications effective from their publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite as: 'A.P.C. Application of ............, Ser. No. ............, Published ............'. STIC Patent Search Room maintains bound volumes of A.P.C. published applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts, Abbreviatures, Defensive Publications, and Statutory Invention Registrations (SIRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts and Abbreviatures are USPTO publications of abandoned applications. Defensive Publications were USPTO publications of provisionally abandoned applications (Defensive Publication program ended May 8, 1985). Statutory Invention Registrations (SIRs) replaced Defensive Publications and are numbered with document category 'H' (beginning with 'H1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defensive Publications and SIRs are included in subclass lists and subscription orders. Distinct numbers were assigned to Defensive Publications published Dec 16, 1969 through Oct 1980; different numbering applies for Defensive Publications on/after Nov 4, 1980. Conversion tables exist for mapping older numbering systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and labeling of paper search files in Technology Centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper search files in TCs are limited to plant-class patents, foreign patent documents, and NPL. Documents are arranged in shoes labeled with class, subclass, and patent ranges; patents arranged numerically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color labels: white = U.S. patents, pink = foreign patents filed by U.S. classifications, blue = non‑patent literature, yellow = foreign patents filed by IPC. Foreign patents may be available in a 'foreign patent art collection' with 'FOR' subclasses (e.g., 'FOR 000' for class-related foreign documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and placement rules for foreign patent documents and nonpatent publications
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of a U.S. patent is designated 'original' and filed in a specific subclass; other copies may be cross-referenced in additional subclasses. Nonpatent publications or photocopies with many disclosures for a subclass should be filed in shoes following foreign patents or at the bottom of the last shoe of foreign patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reclassification projects after Oct 1, 1995, many foreign patents have not been reclassified into new U.S. schedules and are instead in the foreign patent art collection; 'FOR' subclasses preserve former classification structure and include parent subclass references in parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual of Classification is the key to USPC use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual of Classification (MoC) is the key to the U.S. Patent Classification System and contains class and subclass titles, definitions, notes, indices and class schedules; it is updated every two months and archived in PDF semiannually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Manual as a key to class/subclass definitions and appended notes rather than relying solely on brief titles. The MoC includes: Overview, Classes by related subject matter, Classes Arranged by Art Unit (CAAU), Classes Arranged Numerically with Art Unit and Search Room Locations (CAN), Classes Alphabetically (CAA), and Class Schedules for utility/design/plant classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and interpretation of definition notes and 'See or Search' notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition notes either (A) supplement definitions by explaining terms or giving examples or (B) are 'See or Search' notes referring to related disclosures in other classes/subclasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'See or Search' notes help users decide to include or exclude areas and suggest additional fields of search but are not exhaustive or limiting; reviewers should also check search notes of parent subclasses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index to the U.S. Patent Classification System (USPC) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Index is an alphabetic listing of technical/common terms referring to specific classes/subclasses and is used as an initial entry to the classification system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Index should not be considered exhaustive; all appropriate class schedules and the associated definitions/notes should be scanned even if the Index points to a specific subclass. Suggestions for index changes should be sent to the TC classification contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online classification and search tools and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification/Home Pages (Internet and Intranet), Patent Classification Retrieval System (PCRS), Classification Insight (LAN), Cassis DVD-ROM series, and other USPTO tools provide classification schedules, definitions, concordances, and searchable PDFs linked to the Patent Full‑Text and Image Database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Classification Home Page to integrate with the Patent Full‑Text and Image Database to browse patents in subclasses; PCRS provides Original and Cross-Reference classification info updated bimonthly. Classification Insight contains multiple resources (patent classification data, schedules, concordances, PDFs). Cassis DVD-ROM series and vendor tools give additional patent information and search capabilities.
